artworks.title: 1899 Winton Motor Carriage
artworks.artist: Winton Motor Carriage Company, Cleveland, Ohio (1897-1924)
artworks.medium: Engine: 1-cylinder, horizontal configuration, variable inlet valve actuated by compressed air, 142 cu. in./2.3 l.; 9 horsepower
artworks.galleryName: J.K. Lilly III Automobile Gallery (a round Shaker-style barn) & Heald Conference Center: From Carriage to Classic
artworks.description: A close look at this car makes it clear why early automobiles were called “horseless carriages.” The horse and buggy is reflected in its design, its height, its wooden body, and even in its name. Most early automobiles used tillers for steering. Alexander Winton was arguably the most important early American maker of automobiles. He started as a bicycle maker, then began experimenting with early automobiles.
artworks.exhibition: From Carriage to Classic: How Automobiles Transformed America (April 25 – October 18, 2026)

artworks.title: 1904 Oldsmobile Runabout
artworks.medium: Engine: 1-cylinder, horizontal configuration, 118 cu.in./2 l.; 7 horsepower
artworks.galleryName: J.K. Lilly III Automobile Gallery (a round Shaker-style barn) & Heald Conference Center: From Carriage to Classic
artworks.description: Ransom Eli Olds experimented with steam, electric, and gasoline automobiles early in his career. He built a new factory in 1900, with as many as six different models in the prototype stage. A fire at the plant in March 1901 destroyed all but one which was saved by fleeing workers. With his hand forced by fate, Olds began production of the only one left, the Runabout. The auto, nicknamed the “Curved-dash Olds,” was an immediate success.
artworks.exhibition: From Carriage to Classic: How Automobiles Transformed America (April 25 – October 18, 2026)

artworks.title: 1908 Waltham-Orient Buckboard
artworks.medium: Engine: 1-cylinder overhead valve configuration, 35 cu.in./.6 l.; 4 horsepower
artworks.galleryName: J.K. Lilly III Automobile Gallery (a round Shaker-style barn) & Heald Conference Center: From Carriage to Classic
artworks.description: In the early days of motoring, lightweight and inexpensive autos like this one were very popular. Referred to as “buckboards” because of their wooden construction, they were designed to withstand the rigors of traveling on the muddy and rutted roads of the time. Buckboards were particularly attractive to country doctors, farmers, and others forced to travel in less-than-ideal conditions. The first buckboards released by Waltham in 1902 were crude with no suspension, tiller steering, and a very basic wooden body.
artworks.exhibition: From Carriage to Classic: How Automobiles Transformed America (April 25 – October 18, 2026)

artworks.title: 1909 White Steam Car Model M
artworks.medium: Engine: 2-cylinder double acting, with a steam vapor recovery system, 120 cu.in./2 l.; 40 horsepower
artworks.galleryName: J.K. Lilly III Automobile Gallery (a round Shaker-style barn) & Heald Conference Center: From Carriage to Classic
artworks.description: In 1909, newly-elected president William Howard Taft turned the White House stables into a garage and purchased four automobiles: two Pierce- Arrows, a Baker electric, and this White Steamer. He was the first president to be officially transported by automobile, rather than by horse and carriage. This car proved to be a favorite. The president would use bursts of steam to ward off pesky press photographers. Taft firmly believed that the automobile was the future of transportation in America.
artworks.exhibition: From Carriage to Classic: How Automobiles Transformed America (April 25 – October 18, 2026)

artworks.title: 1910 Cadillac Model 30 Roadster
artworks.artist: Cadillac Motor Car Company, Detroit, Michigan (1903-present)
artworks.medium: Engine: 4-cylinder, individually cast configuration, 286 cu. in./4.7 l.; 33 horsepower
artworks.galleryName: J.K. Lilly III Automobile Gallery (a round Shaker-style barn) & Heald Conference Center: From Carriage to Classic
artworks.description: Prior to 1908, automobiles were built by hand with non-interchangeable parts. Each part required time-consuming filing and hand-fitting. Cadillac revolutionized this process by introducing precision machine work and standardization. Each part was exactly the same size as the next and could be easily interchanged.
artworks.exhibition: From Carriage to Classic: How Automobiles Transformed America (April 25 – October 18, 2026)

artworks.title: 1910 Peerless Model 27 Roadster
artworks.medium: Engine: 4-cylinder T-head configuration cast in pairs, 410 cu. in./6.7 l.; 30 horsepower
artworks.galleryName: J.K. Lilly III Automobile Gallery (a round Shaker-style barn) & Heald Conference Center: From Carriage to Classic
artworks.description: In the early days of motoring, Peerless, Packard, and Pierce-Arrow were known as “the three Ps.” This great trio of American car manufacturers competed to produce the most highly regarded luxury vehicles of their day. Early ads of the time claimed the Peerless defeated other American and foreign cars in “speed, hill-climbing, and endurance.” Like a number of successful automakers, Peerless had manufacturing origins far removed from transportation vehicles.
artworks.exhibition: From Carriage to Classic: How Automobiles Transformed America (April 25 – October 18, 2026)

artworks.title: 1910 Sears Model P Surrey
artworks.medium: Engine: Horizontally-opposed air cooled 2-cylinder, flathead configuration, 107 cu. in./1.8 l.; 14 horsepower
artworks.galleryName: J.K. Lilly III Automobile Gallery (a round Shaker-style barn) & Heald Conference Center: From Carriage to Classic
artworks.description: For many rural Americans in the early 1900s, the mail order catalog was their lifeline to the outside world. With this in mind, Sears, Roebuck & Company marketed this car by special catalog from 1909-1912. Buyers could pick it up in Chicago or have it delivered by train to the closest depot. All they had to do was uncrate the car, do some minor assembly, add oil (included in the shipment) and gasoline and drive it home. Rural residents were not automobile fans at first.
artworks.exhibition: From Carriage to Classic: How Automobiles Transformed America (April 25 – October 18, 2026)

artworks.title: 1912 Mercer Raceabout
artworks.artist: Mercer Automobile Company, Trenton, New Jersey (1910-1925)
artworks.medium: Engine: 4-cylinder T-head configuration, 300 cu. in./5 l.; 58 horsepower
artworks.galleryName: J.K. Lilly III Automobile Gallery (a round Shaker-style barn) & Heald Conference Center: From Carriage to Classic
artworks.description: The Mercer Raceabout is considered the most-prized original American sports car. Known for its advanced design, magnificent handling, and high speed, these cars won five of six races they entered in 1911. Mercers came with the unheard of guarantee that each Raceabout would achieve a minimum of 70 miles per hour without modification on public roads, at a time when most cars had trouble reaching the 45-50 mile per hour range!
artworks.exhibition: From Carriage to Classic: How Automobiles Transformed America (April 25 – October 18, 2026)

artworks.title: 1912 Packard 1-48 Victoria
artworks.artist: Packard Motor Car Company, Detroit, Michigan (1899-1958)
artworks.medium: Engine: 6-cylinder T-head configuration, cast in 3 blocks, 525 cu. in./8.6 l.; 74 horsepower
artworks.galleryName: J.K. Lilly III Automobile Gallery (a round Shaker-style barn) & Heald Conference Center: From Carriage to Classic
artworks.placeNote: Price new: unknown due to custom coachwork ($5,200 with factory body).
artworks.description: Packard Motor Company made autos of superb craftsmanship, spare-no-expense materials, advanced engineering and elegant style, and quickly became one of America’s premier auto manufacturers. Along with Pierce-Arrow and Peerless, they were a proud member of the “Three Ps,” a nickname for the top carmakers of the time. This custom-built car was owned by Mrs. Theodate Pope Riddle, one of America’s foremost female architects.
artworks.exhibition: From Carriage to Classic: How Automobiles Transformed America (April 25 – October 18, 2026)

artworks.title: 1913 Ford Model T Touring
artworks.medium: Engine: 4-cylinder flathead configuration, 177 cu. in./2.90 l.; 20 horsepower
artworks.galleryName: J.K. Lilly III Automobile Gallery (a round Shaker-style barn) & Heald Conference Center: From Carriage to Classic
artworks.description: After Henry Ford developed earlier Models R and S, he decided to design a new car. In a secluded room in the Ford factory, Ford and his engineers designed the Model T. He made sure the new car was easy to drive, simple to maintain, rugged enough to traverse rough roads, and inexpensive for most families to afford. Once the public got a taste of the Model T, they used them for just about everything – for work and for pleasure. Farmers converted their Model Ts into tractors or used them to power other machinery.
artworks.exhibition: From Carriage to Classic: How Automobiles Transformed America (April 25 – October 18, 2026)

artworks.title: 1913 Pope-Hartford Model 33 Roadster
artworks.artist: The Pope Manufacturing Company, Hartford, Connecticut (1904-1914)
artworks.medium: Engine: 4-cylinder overhead valve configuration, 350 cu. in./5.7 l.; 50 horsepower
artworks.galleryName: J.K. Lilly III Automobile Gallery (a round Shaker-style barn) & Heald Conference Center: From Carriage to Classic
artworks.description: In 1895, Colonel Albert Pope, an early bicycle proponent and manufacturer, noticed that bicycles were losing ground to a new leisure activity for the wealthy, the horseless carriage. Pope hired an engineer and they began to experiment. Starting with a manufacturing empire already in place, Pope had an enormous advantage over others who were working toward the same goal. By 1899, the Pope Manufacturing Company had become the largest car producer in America, having produced over 500 vehicles.
artworks.exhibition: From Carriage to Classic: How Automobiles Transformed America (April 25 – October 18, 2026)

artworks.title: 1915 Ford Model T Roadster Pickup
artworks.artist: T Ford Motor Company, Detroit Michigan (1903-present)
artworks.medium: Engine: Four cylinder flathead configuration, 176 cu.in./3.75 l.; 20 horsepower
artworks.galleryName: J.K. Lilly III Automobile Gallery (a round Shaker-style barn) & Heald Conference Center: From Carriage to Classic
artworks.description: In 1915 Henry Ford had not yet begun to offer the Model T in a truck configuration. If a buyer wanted a pickup, they bought a bare chassis from Ford, then purchased a cab and body from an aftermarket supplier. Although smaller than many of the commercial trucks made at the time, the Model T was adapted for many industries due to its affordable price, durability, and wide availability.
artworks.exhibition: From Carriage to Classic: How Automobiles Transformed America (April 25 – October 18, 2026)

artworks.title: 1916 Simplex Crane Model 5 Touring
artworks.artist: Simplex Automobile Company, New Brunswick, New Jersey (1907-1924)
artworks.medium: Engine: 6 cylinder flathead configuration, cast in two blocks, 565 cu. in. / 9.3 l.; 110 horsepower
artworks.galleryName: J.K. Lilly III Automobile Gallery (a round Shaker-style barn) & Heald Conference Center: From Carriage to Classic
artworks.description: The Simplex Automobile Company built costly, ultra-high quality automobiles, first from 1915-1919 and then again from 1922-1924. The designer was MIT graduate Henry Crane, an award-winning designer of powerboats. His plans called for a huge engine and the best alloys of steel and aluminum. These cars appealed to older, wealthy families. Frederick William Vanderbilt owned one. The Rockefellers owned several. As with many luxury vehicles at this time, Simplex cars were available in chassis form only.
artworks.exhibition: From Carriage to Classic: How Automobiles Transformed America (April 25 – October 18, 2026)

artworks.title: 1917 Milburn Light Electric
artworks.medium: Engine: General Electric, powered by thirteen 6-volt batteries; 3.36 horsepower
artworks.galleryName: J.K. Lilly III Automobile Gallery (a round Shaker-style barn) & Heald Conference Center: From Carriage to Classic
artworks.description: Milburn was one of the more successful makers of electric automobiles. Their cars were priced low and were light weight. The company also offered a unique a battery pack on rollers, allowing fresh batteries to be installed quickly. Eliminating the downtime required for re-charging made the Milburn much more versatile and useful than other electric cars.
artworks.exhibition: From Carriage to Classic: How Automobiles Transformed America (April 25 – October 18, 2026)

artworks.title: 1919 Pierce-Arrow Model 48 Touring
artworks.artist: Pierce-Arrow Motor Car Co., Buffalo, New York (1901-1938)
artworks.medium: Engine: 6 cylinder T-head configuration with 4 valves per cylinder, 525 cu. in. / 8.6 l.; 48 horsepower
artworks.galleryName: J.K. Lilly III Automobile Gallery (a round Shaker-style barn) & Heald Conference Center: From Carriage to Classic
artworks.description: Between 1905 and 1925, there were thousands of automobile manufacturers in the United States. The most successful were those that had manufactured something else before they began making cars. George N. Pierce started by producing birdcages, progressed to bicycles, and eventually automobiles in 1901. From the start, Pierce built cars of impeccable quality and workmanship, making extensive use of aluminum, bronze, and copper.
artworks.exhibition: From Carriage to Classic: How Automobiles Transformed America (April 25 – October 18, 2026)

artworks.title: 1922 Ford Model T Howe Pumper
artworks.medium: Engine: 4-cylinder flathead, 177 cu. in./2.9 l.; 20 Thank you to our dedicated team of volunteers! Jon Capistron Jon Elmendorf Phil Forte Elliot Friend David Greenman Rick Mignone Don McKennit Craig Smith horsepower
artworks.galleryName: J.K. Lilly III Automobile Gallery (a round Shaker-style barn) & Heald Conference Center: From Carriage to Classic
artworks.placeNote: Price new: unknown due to conversion.
artworks.description: This fire truck was put into service in New Portland, Maine, a community of about 800, in June of 1922. Big fire trucks were not practical, both in size and expense, for rural communities. To fill this need, fire equipment manufacturers built lighter-duty apparatus on car chassis, in this case that of a Model T. The Howe Fire Apparatus Company installed a large three-cycle piston pump that could move water at a rate of 250 gallons a minute.
artworks.exhibition: From Carriage to Classic: How Automobiles Transformed America (April 25 – October 18, 2026)

artworks.title: 1924 Brewster Brougham
artworks.artist: Brewster & Co., Long Island City, NY (1915-1925)
artworks.medium: Engine: 4-cylinder Knight patent sleeve valve configuration, 276 cu. in. / 4.5 l.; 30 horsepower
artworks.galleryName: J.K. Lilly III Automobile Gallery (a round Shaker-style barn) & Heald Conference Center: From Carriage to Classic
artworks.description: Brewster & Company began in 1810 as a producer of high-quality horse-drawn carriages for wealthy clients. They made their first auto body in 1896, and continued building car bodies for American and imported European chassis until the outbreak of World War I in Europe. With their supply of chassis threatened, Brewster turned to making their own complete automobiles. Thanks to their smooth and quiet sleeve valve engine, Brewsters were an excellent choice for city driving.
artworks.exhibition: From Carriage to Classic: How Automobiles Transformed America (April 25 – October 18, 2026)

artworks.title: 1925 Franklin Sport Runabout
artworks.artist: Franklin Automobile Company, Syracuse, New York (1901-1934)
artworks.medium: Engine: Air-cooled 6-cylinder overhead valve configuration, 188 cu. in./3.3 l.; 35 horsepower
artworks.galleryName: J.K. Lilly III Automobile Gallery (a round Shaker-style barn) & Heald Conference Center: From Carriage to Classic
artworks.description: From its beginnings in 1910, Franklin was an innovative automaker, especially well known for its trademark air-cooled engines. Franklin made the most successful air-cooled cars in history until the Volkswagen Beetle came along. This car’s false radiator serves no purpose other than to give it the appearance of a water-cooled car. Before 1925, Franklins were more renowned for their reliability, craftsmanship and superb riding qualities than for their style. That changed in 1925 with a new line of cars designed by J.
artworks.exhibition: From Carriage to Classic: How Automobiles Transformed America (April 25 – October 18, 2026)

artworks.title: 1925 Rickenbacker 8 Coupe
artworks.medium: Engine: Straight eight flat head configuration, 269 cu. in./4.4 l.; 80 Thank you to our dedicated team of volunteers! Jon Capistron Jon Elmendorf Phil Forte Elliot Friend David Greenman Rick Mignone Don McKennit Craig Smith horsepower
artworks.galleryName: J.K. Lilly III Automobile Gallery (a round Shaker-style barn) & Heald Conference Center: From Carriage to Classic
artworks.description: Eddie Rickenbacker led a remarkable life. He started out as a famous race car driver, then became a flying ace during World War I. Following the war, he partnered with three auto executives to release a car bearing his name. His flying squadron’s “Hat in the Ring” symbol became the company’s emblem. Rickenbackers were mechanically innovative thanks to Eddie’s expertise as a race car driver. Rickenbacker became the first company to offer four-wheel brakes as standard equipment on moderately priced cars.
artworks.exhibition: From Carriage to Classic: How Automobiles Transformed America (April 25 – October 18, 2026)

artworks.title: 1930 Cadillac V-16 Convertible Coupe
artworks.artist: General Motors, Detroit, Michigan, Cadillac Motor division (1930-present)
artworks.medium: Engine: 16 cylinders in two banks of 8, overhead valve configuration, 452 cu. in./7.4 l.; 165 horsepower
artworks.galleryName: J.K. Lilly III Automobile Gallery (a round Shaker-style barn) & Heald Conference Center: From Carriage to Classic
artworks.description: In the 1920s Packard and Cadillac were locked in fierce competition to make the largest engine possible. Packard had released a V-12, prompting Cadillac to work in secrecy to develop a V-16. The final design called for two V-8s fused together with separate fuel and ignition systems for each side. Cadillac debuted their new, powerful engine at the New York Auto Show on January 4, 1930, just a few months after the stock market crash that brought on the Great Depression.
artworks.exhibition: From Carriage to Classic: How Automobiles Transformed America (April 25 – October 18, 2026)

artworks.title: 1930 Duesenberg Model J Derham Tourster
artworks.medium: Engine: Straight 8, overhead valve configuration actuated by dual overhead camshafts, 4 valves per cylinder, 427 cu. in./6.9 l.; 265 horsepower
artworks.galleryName: J.K. Lilly III Automobile Gallery (a round Shaker-style barn) & Heald Conference Center: From Carriage to Classic
artworks.description: When E.L. Cord purchased Duesenberg in 1926, he challenged mechanical engineer Fred Duesenberg to design the best car in the world. Fred set out to build an automotive masterpiece. The resulting Model J had superlative engineering and custom body styling. Duesenbergs are one of the costliest and most coveted cars ever produced in America. They inspired the saying “It’s a duesie”!
artworks.exhibition: From Carriage to Classic: How Automobiles Transformed America (April 25 – October 18, 2026)

artworks.title: 1931 Ford Model A Deluxe Phaeton
artworks.medium: Engine: 4-cylinder flathead, 200 cu. in./3.3 l.; 40 horsepower
artworks.galleryName: J.K. Lilly III Automobile Gallery (a round Shaker-style barn) & Heald Conference Center: From Carriage to Classic
artworks.description: Model As were cars Henry Ford never wanted to build. He firmly believed that the Model T was the ultimate car. He changed his mind only when flashier, more modern cars made by his competitors cut deeply into the Model T’s sales. Ford shut down his factories for nearly a year while his company worked to create a worthy successor to the T. During that time, car sales everywhere slowed almost to a halt as people waited to see the “new Ford” before buying.
artworks.exhibition: From Carriage to Classic: How Automobiles Transformed America (April 25 – October 18, 2026)

artworks.title: 1932 Auburn Boattail Speedster
artworks.medium: Engine: Lycoming straight 8 flathead configuration, 268 cu. in./4.4 l.; 100 horsepower
artworks.galleryName: J.K. Lilly III Automobile Gallery (a round Shaker-style barn) & Heald Conference Center: From Carriage to Classic
artworks.description: The Auburn Company was founded in 1900 and enjoyed early success. Like many manufacturers, it experienced intense competition in the early 1920s. Near failure, the company was rescued by E.L. Cord. He changed production to offer great-looking cars with fancy features, while keeping prices reasonable with thrifty manufacturing standards. The success of Auburn helped Cord build a financial base to acquire Duesenberg and Lycoming Engine, and then to launch a new car bearing his name.
artworks.exhibition: From Carriage to Classic: How Automobiles Transformed America (April 25 – October 18, 2026)

artworks.title: 1935 Ford Phaeton
artworks.medium: Engine: V-8 flathead, 221 cu. in./3.6 l.; 85 horsepower
artworks.galleryName: J.K. Lilly III Automobile Gallery (a round Shaker-style barn) & Heald Conference Center: From Carriage to Classic
artworks.description: For Ford, the 1935 model year included a complete refresh over previous models. This car had a more modern appearance; the prominent grille was complemented by the more integrated fenders. This gave the car a pleasing streamlined appearance. Few motoring enthusiasts would disagree with Ford’s slogan for the year: “Greater Beauty, Greater Comfort, and Greater Safety.” This particular car was kept in one Cape Cod family for 78 years. In 1932, when Paul Talbot was 13, he asked his parents for a bicycle.
artworks.exhibition: From Carriage to Classic: How Automobiles Transformed America (April 25 – October 18, 2026)

artworks.title: 1936 Cord 810 Westchester
artworks.medium: Engine: Lycoming flathead V-8 configuration, 289 cu. in./4.7 l.; 125 horsepower
artworks.galleryName: J.K. Lilly III Automobile Gallery (a round Shaker-style barn) & Heald Conference Center: From Carriage to Classic
artworks.description: The 1936 Cord is counted as the most striking and innovative car of its time. Mechanically it was way ahead of its peers. Cord was the first mass-production auto offered with front-wheel drive. The elimination of the rear drive train allowed the car to be so low, running boards were unnecessary. It also featured an “alligator” style hood hinged at the rear, “coffin” front-end styling, concealed door hinges, and teardrop shaped fenders.
artworks.exhibition: From Carriage to Classic: How Automobiles Transformed America (April 25 – October 18, 2026)

artworks.title: 1962 Chevrolet Corvette
artworks.artist: General Motors, Detroit, Michigan, Chevrolet Division, Corvette production 1953-present
artworks.medium: Engine: 8-cylinder overhead valve configuration, 327 cu. in./5.4 l.; 340 horsepower
artworks.galleryName: J.K. Lilly III Automobile Gallery (a round Shaker-style barn) & Heald Conference Center: From Carriage to Classic
artworks.description: Rivalries between auto manufacturers are not a recent phenomenon. Like early race car rivals Mercer and Stutz, Ford and Chevrolet competed with the Thunderbird and Corvette. The Corvette was based on a 1952 show car and went into production virtually unchanged the following year. Designed by noted automobile stylist Harley Earl, the Corvette was created as an economical sports car for young adults. Although the initial public response was strong, sales figures remained low.
artworks.exhibition: From Carriage to Classic: How Automobiles Transformed America (April 25 – October 18, 2026)
